title: KPI Dashboard Spec — PLG Signals (Signal→Task→Meeting→SQL→Pipeline)
content:
Context
This spec defines the KPI framework + dashboard requirements for the PLG→Sales signal routing project. The goal is to measure end-to-end impact and tune thresholds/messaging while controlling false positives and duplication.

We are explicitly measuring a funnel:
1) Signal emitted (product usage / intent)
2) HubSpot activation (task created + SDR/AE notified / sequence enrollment)
3) Sales action (first touch / reply)
4) Meeting booked/held
5) SQL created (handoff to AE / qualified in CRM)
6) Pipeline created (deal opened + amount)
7) Conversion outcome (won/lost + reasons)

Audience
- Exec: Jordan Blake (CRO) / Sales leaders (Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer)
- Ops: Chris Osei (Product Ops), Isabelle Laurent (Sales Ops), Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
- Systems: David Kim (HubSpot admin), Logan Wright / Mei Lin (pipeline + data)
- SDR program: Grace O’Connor

Non-goals
- This doc does not define the signal thresholds themselves (see PM-412 / threshold analysis sheet).
- This doc does not define HubSpot workflow implementation details (see PM-413 + ENG-2843).

Definitions (canonical)
Key objects
- “Signal Event”: a scored, deduped output event from the scoring service (ENG-2842). Written into HubSpot as a Company Timeline Event and optionally triggers task + sequence enrollment.
- “Activation”: creation of a HubSpot Task (or equivalent CTA) attributable to a Signal Event.
- “First Touch”: first outbound activity after Activation (email sent, call placed, LinkedIn step logged).
- “Meeting”: meeting booked and held with AE/SDR/SE (tracked via HubSpot meeting object or calendar integration).
- “SQL”: Sales Qualified Lead (operational definition below).
- “Pipeline”: Deal created with amount and stage >= “Discovery” (or Redwood equivalent) and associated to the company.

Time windows
- Measurement windows for signals are 7/14/30d usage aggregates; for KPI reporting we use:
  - Activation latency: same-day, 24h, 72h buckets
  - Funnel progression: 14d and 30d look-forward windows from signal timestamp
  - Pipeline & conversion: 90d look-forward window (pilot: track early leading indicators)

Pilot cohort
- Pilot dashboards must support filtering by: pilot_allowlist=true (from routing config) and by “signal_version” (v1, v1.1).

Primary KPIs (north stars)
1) Signal-to-Meeting Rate (S→M)
Definition: % of unique signal activations that result in a meeting booked within 14 days of activation.
Formula: Meetings_booked_14d / Activations
Notes:
- “Unique activation” is deduped at the company + signal_type + dedupe_window level.
- Include meetings booked by SDR or AE; exclude purely inbound demo requests not linked to the activation (see attribution rules).

2) Signal-to-Pipeline Rate (S→P)
Definition: % of unique signal activations that result in a new deal created within 30 days.
Formula: Deals_created_30d / Activations
Notes:
- Deals must be linked to the same company record.
- If multiple deals created, count once per activation; keep a separate metric for multi-deal cases.

3) Signal-attributed Pipeline $ (S→$)
Definition: Sum of deal amount for deals attributed to signals.
Formula: Sum(deal_amount * attribution_weight)
Default weighting in pilot: 1.0 if “signal-sourced”, 0.5 if “signal-influenced” (see below).

4) False Positive Rate (operational)
Definition: % of activations reviewed by SDR/AE that are marked “Not relevant / bad trigger”.
Source: required task outcome field (new HubSpot property) or sequence disposition.
Formula: Bad_trigger_dispositions / Activations_with_disposition
Target (pilot): < 25% within first 2 weeks; < 15% by rollout gate.

5) Duplicate Outreach Rate
Definition: % of companies receiving more than one activation task within a 14-day window for the same signal family.
Formula: Companies_with_2plus_activations_14d_same_family / Companies_with_any_activation
This is a guardrail to protect brand trust.

Secondary KPIs (diagnostics)
A) Coverage + volume
- Signals emitted per day/week, by type and by segment
- Activations per day/week, by owner (SDR/AE), by region
- Suppressed signals per day/week + suppression reason distribution

B) Velocity
- Signal→HubSpot write latency (p50/p90)
- Activation→First touch latency (p50/p90)
- Activation→Meeting booked latency (p50/p90)

C) Sales execution
- First touch rate within SLA
- Sequence enrollment rate (where applicable)
- Reply rate (email) and connect rate (calls), by signal type
- Meeting held rate (booked vs held)

D) Stage quality
- SQL creation rate (meeting→SQL)
- Pipeline creation rate (SQL→deal)
- Win rate and average cycle time (longer-term)

Operational definitions (must be consistent)
Activation
An activation exists when any of the following is created within 1 hour of the signal being written into HubSpot:
- HubSpot Task of type “PLG Signal Follow-up” associated with company
- Enrollment in a defined sequence with a “plg_signal_activation_id” property populated

Meeting (Booked)
A meeting is “booked” when:
- HubSpot meeting object exists OR calendar event is logged as meeting with a Redwood owner, and
- Meeting type is not “support-only” (exclude support escalations unless explicitly marked as expansion qualification)

Meeting (Held)
Held when meeting outcome is “Completed” or has notes logged within 48h after scheduled time.

SQL
For pilot reporting, SQL occurs when:
- A HubSpot lifecycle stage (or custom field) is set to SQL AND
- At least one qualification field is filled: deployment_mode_interest (Dedicated/Private), security_review_needed, region_residency_requirement, or target monthly spend band.
Rationale: avoid counting “curiosity calls” as SQL.

Pipeline
Pipeline is a Deal that:
- Is created within 30 days of activation
- Has an amount > $0 (or is backfilled within 7 days)
- Is in a stage >= Discovery

Attribution rules
We need two attribution lenses: (1) strict “signal-sourced” for causality and (2) broader “signal-influenced” for practical GTM value.

A) Signal-sourced
A deal is signal-sourced if ALL are true:
1) Deal create date is within 30 days of activation date
2) The first logged outbound activity after activation is linked to the company and occurs before the meeting is booked
3) The meeting that led to SQL is within 14 days of activation
4) The deal has a “plg_signal_activation_id” populated (via workflow) OR is explicitly associated via a manual “Attributed to PLG Signal” checkbox (allowed during pilot)

B) Signal-influenced
A deal is signal-influenced if:
- A signal activation exists in the 90 days prior to deal creation AND
- There is any outbound activity from SDR/AE/SE within 7 days of activation (even if a separate inbound event also exists)

C) Pre-existing opportunity suppression
Signals should be suppressed from creating new tasks if there is an active open deal (stage not Closed Won/Lost) OR if account is flagged “CS-managed enterprise”.
For KPI reporting, suppressed signals are still counted as “signals emitted”, but not counted in “activations”.

D) Dedupe window
Default: no more than one activation per company per signal_type per 14 days.
Reporting must include “raw signals” and “deduped signals” so we can detect bugs (e.g., SUP-1932 type incidents).

Segmentation (required filters)
All dashboards must be filterable by:
- Date range (signal timestamp and activation timestamp)
- Pilot allowlist vs full population
- Region (NA/EMEA/APAC) and subregion where known
- Segment (self-serve, mid-market, enterprise if inferred; otherwise employee band: 1–50, 51–200, 201–1000, 1000+)
- Signal type (spend growth, concurrency/burst, rate-limit pain, error-rate pain, security intent, residency intent, pricing page repeat, contact sales)
- Owner (SDR/AE)
- Suppression reason

Dashboards needed (v1)
1) Exec Overview — PLG Signals Impact
Audience: CRO + Sales leadership
Tiles:
- Activations (weekly), Meetings booked (weekly), Deals created (weekly)
- S→M rate (14d look-forward) and S→P rate (30d)
- Signal-attributed pipeline $ (signal-sourced and signal-influenced)
- False positive rate (with trend)
- Top signal types by pipeline $
Notes:
- Include a “data freshness” indicator (last successful pipeline run time) and warning if lag > SLA.

2) Funnel Breakdown — by Signal Type
Audience: Product Ops + SDR leadership
For each signal_type:
- Signals emitted → deduped → activations → first touch → meeting booked → meeting held → SQL → pipeline
- Conversion rates between each stage
- Median/90p time-to-next-step

3) SDR/AE Execution & SLA Dashboard
Audience: SDR manager + Sales Ops
- Activation→first touch within SLA (same day / 24h / 72h)
- Tasks created vs completed (and completion time)
- Dispositions: Connected / No response / Bad trigger / Existing project / Too early / Do not contact
- Meeting booked rate by owner (normalize by activation volume)

4) Suppression & Hygiene Dashboard
Audience: Sales Ops + CS
- Suppressed signals by reason: active opp, CS-managed enterprise, opt-out, do-not-contact, pilot off, residency restricted visibility
- “Should have suppressed but didn’t” audit sample (see data quality checks)
- Duplicate outreach incidents (company-level)

5) Data Quality & Pipeline Health Dashboard (Engineering/Ops)
Audience: Logan/Mei/Data on-call + Biz Systems
- HubSpot write success rate (events/tasks), retry counts, rate limit responses
- Signal pipeline lag (event time to HubSpot timeline time)
- Volume anomaly detection (z-score vs trailing 4 weeks)
- Idempotency collisions / dedupe key error counts
- Dead-letter queue volume (if applicable)

Source of truth + data model notes
Primary sources
- Signal scoring output table/event stream (ENG-2842)
- Aggregated usage windows tables (ENG-2841)
- HubSpot objects: Company, Timeline Events, Tasks, Sequences, Meetings, Deals
- Outreach activities (emails/calls) via HubSpot activity logs

Required IDs/properties to support attribution
We need the following properties on HubSpot records (names tentative; David K to confirm exact property keys):
- company.plg_signal_last_activation_ts
- task.plg_signal_activation_id
- task.plg_signal_type
- task.plg_signal_score
- task.plg_signal_dedupe_key
- task.plg_signal_disposition (required on close)
- deal.plg_signal_attribution (none | sourced | influenced)
- deal.plg_signal_activation_id (nullable)
- company.plg_signal_visibility (standard | restricted)

Data quality checks (must-haves)
These checks should run daily and be reviewed in weekly pilot standup.

1) Completeness: signal→HubSpot write
- Check: % of deduped signals with a matching HubSpot timeline event within 2 hours
- Target: > 99% in steady state; alert if < 97% over 2 consecutive hours

2) Completeness: HubSpot event→activation
- Check: % of timeline events that resulted in a task or sequence enrollment (for signal types configured to activate)
- Explanation: if this drops, workflows may be broken.

3) Dedupe correctness
- Check: no company has >1 activation task for same signal_type within dedupe window
- Exception list: explicit manual override tag “dedupe_override=true” (should be rare)

4) Suppression correctness (audit sample)
- Check: sample 25 activated companies/week; verify no active deal existed at activation time and not CS-managed enterprise
- Output: list of violations with root cause tag (stale deal stage, missing association, incorrect enterprise flag)

5) Owner mapping coverage
- Check: % activations with non-null owner_id assigned; target > 99%
- If owner missing, assign to routing fallback queue and log.

6) Timestamp sanity
- Check: activation_ts >= signal_ts; meeting_ts >= activation_ts; deal_create_ts >= activation_ts
- Flag records that violate and exclude from conversion metrics until fixed.

7) Amount hygiene
- Check: % deals created with amount = 0 after 7 days
- Action: follow up with Sales Ops to enforce hygiene or backfill rules.

8) Opt-out / DNC compliance
- Check: no activation tasks created for companies flagged opt_out=true or do_not_contact=true
- Alert severity: high (privacy/compliance)

Reporting cadence + stakeholders
- Weekly (pilot): 30-min review with Product Ops + Sales leadership + SDR owner
  - Focus: volumes, false positives, meeting rate, top reasons for “bad trigger”, threshold tuning requests
- Biweekly: Exec readout (Jordan) summarizing pipeline $, wins/losses, and operational issues
- Monthly: attribution + ROI deep dive once sample size is sufficient

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Which meeting definition do we standardize on for exec reporting: booked or held? Proposal: exec uses booked + held side-by-side.
2) How do we handle multi-signal exposures (e.g., spend growth + security intent)? Proposal: last-touch among signals within 30 days for sourced; multi-touch for influenced with weights.
3) How do we incorporate marketing web intent (pricing page repeats) without double-counting lifecycle/email nurture? Proposal: treat as a separate signal family and require a higher score threshold; report separately.

Next steps
- David Kim: confirm exact HubSpot property keys + where each is populated (workflow vs API writer).
- Mei Lin: confirm tables/fields available in analytics for dashboards + implement daily DQ checks.
- Grace O’Connor: finalize required dispositions list + ensure SDR process includes disposition completion.
- Chris Osei / Tyler Benson: align on final attribution logic to use in exec dashboard (sourced vs influenced).

Changelog
- 2025-02-12: v0 created (Chris)
- 2025-02-24: added sourced vs influenced attribution; added suppression/hygiene dashboard (Tyler/Isabelle feedback)
- 2025-03-11: tightened definitions for SQL + meeting held; added DQ checks for opt-out and dedupe (Security + SUP-1932 learnings)
